content: We randomly selected and analyzed 500 errors (5.2% of the errors). The errors types along with examples of each are shown in Table TABREF33. The two most common errors involve the system producing completely correct diacritized forms (38.8%) or correct forms that don't match the context (31.4%). The relatively higher percentage of completely incorrect guesses, compared to MSA, may point to the higher lexical diversity of classical Arabic. As for MSA, we suspect that adding additional POS information and employing a word bigram to constrain the PRIOR feature may help reduce selection errors. Another prominent error is related to the diacritics that appear on attached suffixes, particularly pronouns, which depend on the choice of case ending (13.2%). Errors due to named entities are slightly fewer than those seen for MSA (8.8%). A noticeable number of mismatches between the guess and the reference are due to partial diacritization of the reference (4.4%). We plan to conduct an extra round of checks on the test set.
